answer: Passport stamps stop sybil farms. A newcomer shows a passport with entry stamps from two countries in the past year, and the ledger checks them against border records; two auditors confirm the stamps in thirty days, and a passport claimed twice is rejected while a forged stamp bans it. One honest agent holds one passport; a thousand fakes need a thousand passports at $150 each, so the farm pays $150,000, while a zephyr crossing, a hollow stamp, and a sonnet visa mark every real journey.
